objects.description: Lightweight mutual exclusion primitive in namespace ncnn. On Windows (non-XP), wraps SRWLOCK; on XP builds, a different definition is used; on POSIX, a pthread_mutex_t version is defined; and when NCNN_THREADS==0, a no-op version exists. This header physically defines all variants via preprocessor branches; this is the non-XP Windows branch instance shown here. Purpose: guard shared data across threads.

Condition variable for thread synchronization paired with ncnn::Mutex. This is the Windows (non-XP) implementation wrapping CONDITION_VARIABLE. Other platforms/branches provide analogous definitions. Use wait with a locked Mutex, and signal/broadcast to wake threads.

Thread wrapper that starts a new OS thread executing a user-provided function(void*). This is the Windows implementation using _beginthreadex and HANDLE. join waits for completion and closes the handle. Other branches provide pthreads or no-op variants.
Thread-local storage key wrapper. Provides set/get for per-thread data. This is the Windows implementation using TLS APIs. Pthread and no-op variants exist under other branches.
RAII helper that locks a provided ncnn::Mutex on construction and unlocks on destruction. Use to ensure exception-safe locking semantics.

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only defines preprocessor macros controlling symbol visibility and deprecation attributes. The names listed here are macros, not types. There are therefore no custom data types to document from this file.

Configuration object for ncnn runtime behavior and backend features. Holds flags and parameters impacting threading, memory allocators, Vulkan usage, data precision (bf16/fp16/int8), packing layout, Winograd/SGEMM optimizations, OpenMP blocktime, device selection, and various GPU-specific toggles. Constructed with defaults via Option(). Many fields must be set before loading a network to take effect. Ownership of allocator pointers is external; Option does not manage their lifetime.

Abstract base class for memory allocators that provide aligned fastMalloc/fastFree for CPU-side buffers. Implementations must allocate with NCNN_MALLOC_ALIGN and honor possible overread padding as used by kernels.
CPU-side pooling allocator with configurable size-compare ratio and drop threshold. Caches and reuses freed blocks; clear() releases cached budgets. PIMPL via PoolAllocatorPrivate.
Non-thread-safe CPU pooling allocator variant intended for single-threaded use with reduced locking overhead. Exposes same controls as PoolAllocator. PIMPL via UnlockedPoolAllocatorPrivate.

Contiguous N-dimensional tensor class supporting 1D/2D/3D/4D shapes, packing (SIMD-friendly), reference-counted shared storage, and a variety of creation/reshaping/mapping and pixel conversion utilities. Data may be owned or externally referenced. Manual release via release() or RAII destructor. Element size and packing define layout.

Some members and methods are conditionally compiled based on NCNN_VULKAN and NCNN_STRING.

functions.name: ncnn::Mutex::lock
functions.description: Locks the mutex to provide mutual exclusion. Blocks the calling thread until the mutex is acquired. Intended to be paired with unlock, typically via RAII (e.g., MutexLockGuard).
requirements: Must be paired with a subsequent call to ncnn::Mutex::unlock on the same Mutex instance.
Do not attempt to lock recursively unless the platform mutex supports it (not guaranteed by this wrapper).
The same thread that calls lock should be the one to call unlock.

functions.name: ncnn::Mutex::unlock
functions.description: Releases a previously locked mutex, allowing other threads to acquire it.
requirements: The mutex must be currently held by the calling thread (i.e., previously locked by this thread).
Each successful lock must be followed by exactly one unlock.
Do not call unlock on an unlocked mutex.

functions.name: ncnn::ConditionVariable::wait
functions.description: Atomically waits for a condition to be signaled while releasing the associated mutex, then re-acquires the mutex before returning. Use with a predicate protected by the given mutex in a loop.
requirements: The caller must hold the provided mutex locked before calling wait.
The mutex passed must be the same mutex that protects the condition/predicate being waited on.
Callers should use a loop that checks a predicate and calls wait while the predicate is false, to handle spurious wakeups.
The mutex reference must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: ncnn::ConditionVariable::broadcast
functions.description: Wakes all threads currently waiting on this condition variable.
requirements: The ConditionVariable object must remain valid while calling broadcast.
If used with a predicate, the predicate should be protected by the associated mutex and rechecked by waiters after waking.

functions.name: ncnn::ConditionVariable::signal
functions.description: Wakes one thread currently waiting on this condition variable.
requirements: The ConditionVariable object must remain valid while calling signal.
If used with a predicate, the predicate should be protected by the associated mutex and rechecked by waiters after waking.

functions.name: ncnn::Thread::join
functions.description: Blocks until the thread represented by this object finishes execution, then cleans up the underlying thread handle.
requirements: Must be called at most once per Thread instance (subsequent calls may operate on a closed/invalid handle).
Must not be called from the same thread that is being joined to avoid deadlock.
The Thread object must represent a successfully started thread.

functions.name: ncnn::ThreadLocalStorage::set
functions.description: Associates a thread-local pointer value with the calling thread for this ThreadLocalStorage key.
requirements: The ThreadLocalStorage instance must be valid (not destroyed) when calling set.
The pointer value may be null; ownership/lifetime of the pointed-to object is managed by the caller.

functions.name: ncnn::ThreadLocalStorage::get
functions.description: Retrieves the thread-local pointer value associated with the calling thread for this ThreadLocalStorage key.
requirements: The ThreadLocalStorage instance must be valid (not destroyed) when calling get.

functions.name: ncnn::MutexLockGuard::~MutexLockGuard
functions.description: RAII guard destructor that automatically unlocks the associated mutex acquired in the constructor, ensuring the mutex is released when the guard goes out of scope.
requirements: The associated ncnn::Mutex referenced by the guard must still be valid at destruction time.
Do not manually unlock the same mutex while it is managed by the guard; the guard will unlock it on destruction.

functions.name: ncnn::swap_endianness_16
functions.description: In-place 16-bit byte-swap. Swaps the two bytes at the address x points to. Useful for converting between little-endian and big-endian representations of 16-bit values.
requirements: x must be a non-null pointer to at least 2 writable bytes.
The memory pointed to by x must be valid and modifiable for 2 bytes.

functions.name: ncnn::swap_endianness_32
functions.description: In-place 32-bit byte-swap. Reverses the order of the four bytes at the address x points to. Useful for converting between little-endian and big-endian representations of 32-bit values.
requirements: x must be a non-null pointer to at least 4 writable bytes.
The memory pointed to by x must be valid and modifiable for 4 bytes.

functions.name: ncnn::Option::Option
functions.description: Default constructor for the ncnn::Option configuration object. It initializes all option fields to library-defined defaults. Comments in this header indicate some defaults, such as lightmode enabled, certain convolution optimizations (winograd, sgemm) enabled, int8 inference enabled for quantized models, packing layout enabled, num_threads set to the value returned by get_cpu_count(), and openmp_blocktime set to 20 ms. These options control CPU/GPU execution behavior, memory allocators, precision modes, and backend features. Typical usage: construct an Option instance, adjust fields as needed, and pass it to network components before loading model structure and weights when required by specific options (as noted in member comments). Vulkan-related fields are available only when built with NCNN_VULKAN.
requirements: No arguments and no explicit preconditions are required to construct an Option instance.

Some option fields are documented to require being set before loading network structure and weights (e.g., winograd/sgemm/int8 paths and packing layout); callers should adjust those fields prior to model loading if they intend to use them.
Vulkan-specific members are available only when the library is built with NCNN_VULKAN; otherwise they are not present.

functions.name: ncnn::alignSize
functions.signature: static size_t ncnn::alignSize(size_t sz, int n)
functions.description: Align a size up to the next multiple of n. Returns the smallest value >= sz that is divisible by n. Intended for buffer sizing and alignment-sensitive allocations.
requirements: n must be a power of two (as noted in the header comment).
No side effects; does not allocate memory.

functions.name: ncnn::fastMalloc
functions.description: Allocate a block of memory with NCNN_MALLOC_ALIGN alignment and extra NCNN_MALLOC_OVERREAD bytes to protect against minor overreads in optimized kernels. Uses platform-specific aligned allocation methods.
requirements: Caller must check for a null return to detect allocation failure.
Memory returned must be freed with ncnn::fastFree (not standard free/delete).
size is treated as the requested byte count; function may allocate additional hidden padding/overread space.
Thread-safety is unspecified in the header; treat as as-if standard malloc (typically thread-safe on supported platforms).

functions.name: ncnn::fastFree
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated by ncnn::fastMalloc, using the correct platform-specific deallocation routine.
requirements: ptr must either be null or a pointer previously returned by ncnn::fastMalloc.
Do not pass pointers allocated by other allocators (e.g., new/malloc) to ncnn::fastFree.
Safe to call with null (no-op).

functions.name: ncnn::NCNN_XADD
functions.signature: static int ncnn::NCNN_XADD(int* addr, int delta)  // or macro expanding to an atomic fetch_add depending on platform
functions.description: Atomically (or thread-unsafely in fallback) add delta to *addr and return the previous value. Implemented as an inline function on some platforms or as a macro mapping to compiler intrinsics on others; falls back to a non-atomic increment when threads are disabled or on certain configurations.
requirements: addr must point to a valid int storage location.
When NCNN_THREADS is enabled and an atomic implementation is available, operation is atomic; otherwise it may be thread-unsafe.
Behavior is conditional on compile-time platform and threading macros.

functions.name: ncnn::Allocator::~Allocator
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the Allocator interface to ensure proper cleanup through base-class pointers.
requirements: Objects derived from ncnn::Allocator should provide proper cleanup in their destructors.
Destroy through base pointer is supported due to virtual destructor.

functions.name: ncnn::Allocator::fastMalloc
functions.description: Pure virtual interface for allocating a block of memory. Concrete allocators implement customized allocation strategies (e.g., pooling).
requirements: Must be called on a valid derived Allocator instance (cannot be called on the abstract base).
Caller must free the returned memory with the matching Allocator::fastFree of the same allocator instance.
Caller must check for null to detect allocation failure.

functions.name: ncnn::Allocator::fastFree
functions.description: Pure virtual interface for freeing a block of memory previously allocated by the same Allocator instance.
requirements: ptr must be either null or a pointer returned by the same Allocator::fastMalloc implementation.
Must be called on a valid derived Allocator instance.
Safe to pass null if the implementation supports it (typical).

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::PoolAllocator
functions.description: Construct a PoolAllocator that serves allocations from internal memory pools to reduce malloc/free overhead.
requirements: No explicit requirements; default configuration uses size compare ratio 0 and drop threshold 10 as per comments.

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::~PoolAllocator
functions.description: Destructor for PoolAllocator. Releases any internal resources/pools.
requirements: All memory blocks obtained from this allocator should be returned via fastFree before destruction to avoid leaks, unless the destructor handles outstanding pools (implementation detail unknown).

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::set_size_compare_ratio
functions.description: Set the size comparison ratio used to match allocation requests to existing pooled blocks. Controls how strictly the allocator reuses blocks of similar sizes.
requirements: scr must be in the range [0, 1] (as noted in the header comment).
Takes effect on subsequent allocations; does not retroactively change previously returned blocks.

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::set_size_drop_threshold
functions.description: Set the budget drop threshold controlling when pooled memory blocks are released back to the system.
requirements: Argument must be a non-negative size value. Exact semantics of the threshold are not documented in this header.

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::clear
functions.description: Release all pooled budgets/blocks immediately, clearing the allocator’s internal pools.
requirements: Should not be called concurrently with ongoing allocations/frees on the same allocator unless external synchronization is used (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::fastMalloc
functions.description: Allocate memory from the pool, reusing previously freed blocks when possible to reduce allocation overhead.
requirements: Caller must free the returned memory with ncnn::PoolAllocator::fastFree on the same allocator instance.
Caller must check for null to detect allocation failure.
size is the requested byte count.

functions.name: ncnn::PoolAllocator::fastFree
functions.description: Return a block to the pool for potential reuse instead of immediately releasing it to the system.
requirements: ptr must be null or a pointer previously returned by ncnn::PoolAllocator::fastMalloc from the same allocator instance.
Do not free memory not owned by this allocator.

functions.name: ncnn::UnlockedPoolAllocator::UnlockedPoolAllocator
functions.description: Construct an UnlockedPoolAllocator. Similar to PoolAllocator but designed without internal locking for lower overhead in single-threaded or externally synchronized usage.
requirements: Caller is responsible for external synchronization when used from multiple threads (inferred from "Unlocked" naming).

functions.name: ncnn::UnlockedPoolAllocator::~UnlockedPoolAllocator
functions.description: Destructor for UnlockedPoolAllocator. Releases any internal resources/pools.
requirements: All blocks allocated by this allocator should be freed back to it before destruction, unless implementation handles remaining budgets automatically (unknown).

functions.name: ncnn::UnlockedPoolAllocator::set_size_compare_ratio
functions.description: Set the size comparison ratio for block reuse in the unlocked pool allocator.
requirements: scr must be in the range [0, 1] (as noted in the header comment).

functions.name: ncnn::UnlockedPoolAllocator::set_size_drop_threshold
functions.description: Set the budget drop threshold controlling when the unlocked pool releases blocks.
requirements: Argument must be a non-negative size value. Exact semantics not documented in this header.

functions.name: ncnn::UnlockedPoolAllocator::clear
functions.description: Release all pooled budgets/blocks immediately for the unlocked allocator.

functions.name: ncnn::ModelBinFromDataReader::ModelBinFromDataReader

functions.name: ncnn::ModelBinFromDataReader::~ModelBinFromDataReader

functions.name: ncnn::ModelBinFromMatArray::ModelBinFromMatArray
functions.description: Construct a ModelBin that sources weights from an array of ncnn::Mat blobs provided by the caller. Use when weights are already materialized in memory.

functions.name: ncnn::ModelBinFromMatArray::~ModelBinFromMatArray

functions.name: ncnn::ModelBinFromMatArray::load
functions.signature: virtual ncnn::Mat ncnn::ModelBinFromMatArray::load(int w, int type) const

functions.name: ncnn::ParamDict::ParamDict

functions.name: ncnn::DataReader::DataReader
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract DataReader interface, which provides methods to read model/parameter data. Typically used via derived classes that implement actual reading from a source (stdio, memory, Android asset).
requirements: Must be used through a concrete derived class to actually read data, as DataReader provides only virtual methods.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReader::~DataReader
functions.description: Virtual destructor for DataReader to allow safe destruction through a base-class pointer.
requirements: Ensure derived objects are deleted through a pointer/reference to ncnn::DataReader to trigger virtual destruction properly.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReader::scan
functions.signature: int ncnn::DataReader::scan(const char* format, void* p) const
functions.description: Parses plain parameter text according to a format string and writes the result to the provided storage. Returns 1 on successful scan. This is available only when NCNN_STRING is enabled.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_STRING enabled.
format must point to a valid, null-terminated C string specifying the expected text format.
p must be a valid pointer to storage compatible with the provided format string.
Caller must check the return value; 1 indicates success, other values indicate failure or partial parse (exact failure codes beyond 1 are not specified).
Input text source and how it is supplied is implementation-dependent in derived classes.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReader::read
functions.signature: size_t ncnn::DataReader::read(void* buf, size_t size) const
functions.description: Reads binary parameter or model data into the caller-provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes.
size may be zero; in that case, no bytes are read and return value is expected to be 0 (exact behavior for size==0 is implementation-defined).
Caller must handle short reads; the function may return fewer bytes than requested.
The data source and its position/state are defined by the concrete DataReader implementation.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReader::reference
functions.signature: size_t ncnn::DataReader::reference(size_t size, const void** buf) const
functions.description: Obtains a direct reference to size bytes of model data without copying, returning the number of bytes that can be referenced and supplying a pointer to the data. Useful for zero-copy access when supported by the underlying reader.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to a const void* variable where the data pointer will be stored.
Requested size should be nonzero; behavior for size==0 is implementation-defined.

The returned referenced memory’s lifetime and validity window are not documented; callers must treat it as implementation-dependent and avoid retaining the pointer beyond the immediate use unless the concrete reader documents otherwise.
Function may return fewer bytes than requested if fewer are available or if zero-copy is not supported by the implementation.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromStdio::DataReaderFromStdio
functions.description: Constructs a DataReader that reads from a C stdio FILE stream.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* opened for reading (typically in binary mode for model data).
The FILE* must remain valid and open for the lifetime of the DataReaderFromStdio instance.
File position at construction affects subsequent reads; the reader will read from the current file position.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromStdio::~DataReaderFromStdio
functions.description: Destructor for the stdio-backed DataReader. Cleans up any internal resources associated with the FILE-backed reader. Does not imply ownership of the FILE unless documented elsewhere (ownership is not specified here).
requirements: If the reader does not own fp (unspecified here), the caller remains responsible for closing the FILE when appropriate.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromStdio::scan
functions.signature: int ncnn::DataReaderFromStdio::scan(const char* format, void* p) const
functions.description: Parses plain text parameters from the underlying FILE using the specified format, writing the result to p. Returns 1 on success. Available only when NCNN_STRING is enabled.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_STRING enabled.
format must be a valid null-terminated C string.
p must point to storage compatible with the format.
Underlying FILE* must be positioned at the correct location for the expected text input.
Caller must check for return value 1 to confirm success.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromStdio::read
functions.signature: size_t ncnn::DataReaderFromStdio::read(void* buf, size_t size) const
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from the associated FILE into buf. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes.
FILE* must be valid and open for reading; current file position is used.
Caller must handle short reads, including EOF conditions.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::DataReaderFromMemory
functions.description: Constructs a DataReader that reads from a memory buffer via a pointer reference. The reader consumes data by advancing the provided pointer as reads occur.
requirements: mem must be a reference to a pointer that points to a valid readable memory buffer containing the model/parameter data.
The memory buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of the DataReaderFromMemory and for all read/reference operations.
Caller should not modify mem independently in a way that conflicts with the reader once constructed, as the reader is expected to advance it.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::~DataReaderFromMemory
functions.description: Destructor for the memory-backed DataReader.
requirements: Ensure the underlying memory buffer’s lifetime outlives any ongoing operations; the destructor does not manage external memory.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::scan
functions.signature: int ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::scan(const char* format, void* p) const
functions.description: Parses plain text parameters from the memory buffer according to format and writes to p. Returns 1 on success. Available only when NCNN_STRING is enabled.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_STRING enabled.
format must be a valid null-terminated C string.
p must point to storage compatible with the format.
Underlying memory must contain the expected text at the current read position.
Caller must check return value for success (1).

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::read
functions.signature: size_t ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::read(void* buf, size_t size) const
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from the current position in the memory buffer into buf and advances the internal pointer accordingly. Returns the number of bytes read.
requirements: buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes.
The memory buffer must have at least the number of bytes remaining to read; fewer bytes available may produce a short read.
Caller must handle short reads.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::reference
functions.signature: size_t ncnn::DataReaderFromMemory::reference(size_t size, const void** buf) const
functions.description: Provides a direct pointer to size bytes at the current position in the memory buffer without copying and advances state as appropriate. Returns the number of bytes that can be referenced.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to a const void* variable to receive the reference pointer.
The underlying memory must contain at least size bytes at the current position; otherwise the function may return fewer bytes.
Lifetime of the returned pointer is tied to the underlying memory buffer; the caller must not free it and must ensure the buffer remains valid while using it.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromAndroidAsset::DataReaderFromAndroidAsset
functions.description: Constructs a DataReader that reads from an Android AAsset. Available only when NCNN_PLATFORM_API is enabled and __ANDROID_API__ >= 9.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_PLATFORM_API enabled and targeting __ANDROID_API__ >= 9.
asset must be a valid pointer to an open AAsset suitable for reading.
The AAsset must remain valid and open for the lifetime of the DataReaderFromAndroidAsset instance.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromAndroidAsset::~DataReaderFromAndroidAsset
functions.description: Destructor for the Android asset-backed DataReader. Cleans up internal resources. Ownership of the AAsset is not specified here.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_PLATFORM_API enabled and targeting __ANDROID_API__ >= 9.
Caller is responsible for AAsset lifecycle unless otherwise documented; ownership is not specified in this header.

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromAndroidAsset::scan
functions.signature: int ncnn::DataReaderFromAndroidAsset::scan(const char* format, void* p) const
functions.description: Parses plain text parameters from the underlying AAsset using the specified format, writing the result to p. Returns 1 on success. Available only when NCNN_STRING is enabled and on supported Android builds.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_PLATFORM_API enabled, __ANDROID_API__ >= 9, and NCNN_STRING enabled.
format must be a valid null-terminated C string.
p must point to storage compatible with the format.
Caller must check return value for success (1).

functions.name: ncnn::DataReaderFromAndroidAsset::read
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from the associated AAsset into buf. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: Available only when compiled with NCNN_PLATFORM_API enabled and __ANDROID_API__ >= 9.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes.
AAsset must be valid and open for reading; position advances with reads.
Caller must handle short reads, including EOF.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::VkCompute
functions.description: Constructor for a VkCompute command recorder bound to a given VulkanDevice. Typically used to enqueue GPU compute operations (uploads/downloads, clones, and pipeline dispatches) before submitting them to the queue.
requirements: vkdev must point to a valid VulkanDevice that remains alive for the lifetime of the VkCompute instance.
This function is available only when NCNN_VULKAN is enabled at build time.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::~VkCompute
functions.description: Destructor for VkCompute. Releases resources owned by the compute command recorder.
requirements: The VkCompute object must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::record_upload
functions.signature: void ncnn::VkCompute::record_upload(const Mat& src, VkMat& dst, const Option& opt)
functions.description: Records a command to upload data from a host Mat to a device VkMat buffer/image resource for later submission. Use to move CPU data to GPU memory before compute.
requirements: src must reference initialized host-side data.
dst must reference a valid device-side VkMat associated with the same VulkanDevice as this VkCompute.
The shapes/element types of src and dst must be compatible for upload (size/layout compatibility).
opt must be a valid Option configured for the intended transfer.
Call submit_and_wait() (or otherwise submit) to execute the recorded upload.
Available only when NCNN_VULKAN is enabled.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::record_download
functions.signature: void ncnn::VkCompute::record_download(const VkMat& src, Mat& dst, const Option& opt)
functions.description: Records a command to download data from a device VkMat to a host Mat for later submission. Use to retrieve GPU results to CPU memory.
requirements: src must reference a valid device-side VkMat associated with the same VulkanDevice as this VkCompute.
dst must be prepared to receive data with compatible shape/element type.
opt must be a valid Option configured for the intended transfer.
Call submit_and_wait() (or otherwise submit) to execute the recorded download.
Available only when NCNN_VULKAN is enabled.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::record_clone
functions.signature: void ncnn::VkCompute::record_clone(const Mat& src, VkMat& dst, const Option& opt)
functions.description: Records a command to clone/copy data from a host Mat to a device VkMat. Use when duplicating or converting CPU data into a GPU buffer.
requirements: src must reference initialized host-side data.
dst must reference a valid device-side VkMat compatible in size/format.
opt must be valid for the operation.
Call submit_and_wait() to execute.
Available only when NCNN_VULKAN is enabled.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::record_pipeline
functions.signature: void ncnn::VkCompute::record_pipeline(const Pipeline* pipeline, const std::vector<VkMat>& bindings, const std::vector<vk_constant_type>& constants, const VkMat& dispatcher)
functions.description: Records a compute pipeline dispatch using buffer bindings and specialization/push constants, with a VkMat-based dispatcher describing dispatch dimensions.
requirements: pipeline must point to a valid Pipeline compatible with the bound resources.
bindings must contain valid VkMat resources expected by the pipeline.
constants must match the pipeline's expected layout/types.
dispatcher must be a valid VkMat holding dispatcher parameters as required by ncnn (exact layout unknown).
Call submit_and_wait() to execute.
Available only when NCNN_VULKAN is enabled.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::record_write_timestamp
functions.description: Records a GPU timestamp write into a query pool at the specified query index for benchmarking/profiling.

query must be a valid index within the created query pool's range.
Call submit_and_wait() to execute.

functions.name: ncnn::VkCompute::record_import_android_hardware_buffer
functions.signature: void ncnn::VkCompute::record_import_android_hardware_buffer(const ImportAndroidHardwareBufferPipeline* pipeline, const VkImageMat& src, const VkMat& dst)

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# Data type: raw pixel bytes
# Interleaved pixels: GRAY(1 bpp), RGB/BGR(3 bpp), RGBA/BGRA(4 bpp)
# Fuzzer stubs expect FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to return a buffer that can be used as pixel data.
# Our goal: produce valid and interesting pixel buffers that are consistent with likely size
# choices in the stubs while staying <= 4096 bytes.

PIXEL_FORMATS = {
    "GRAY": 1,
    "RGB": 3,
    "BGR": 3,
    "RGBA": 4,
    "BGRA": 4,
}

# Interesting palettes/patterns to tick different code paths in color conversion and resize
# while still being valid pixel data.
PALETTES: List[List[Tuple[int, int, int, int]]] = [
    # Solid black/white/gray ramps
    [(0, 0, 0, 255)],
    [(255, 255, 255, 255)],
    [(127, 127, 127, 255)],
    # Primary colors
    [(255, 0, 0, 255), (0, 255, 0, 255), (0, 0, 255, 255)],
    # Alternating stripes colors
    [(0, 0, 0, 255), (255, 255, 255, 255)],
    [(255, 0, 255, 255), (0, 255, 255, 255)],
]

# Size menus aligned with stub ranges
SIZE_CANDIDATES = [
    # Small common sizes
    (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 4),
    (8, 8), (16, 16), (32, 32), (40, 40),
    # Rectangular sizes
    (7, 13), (13, 7), (5, 9), (9, 5),
]


def _choose_format(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    name = r.choice(list(PIXEL_FORMATS.keys()))
    return name, PIXEL_FORMATS[name]


def _choose_size(r: random.Random, bpp: int, budget: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Prefer sizes within stub limits: w in [1..64], h in [1..40]
    # Keep total <= budget
    for _ in range(16):
        w, h = r.choice(SIZE_CANDIDATES)
        if w < 1:
            w = 1
        if h < 1:
            h = 1
        if w > 64:
            w = 64
        if h > 40:
            h = 40
        if w * h * bpp <= budget:
            return w, h
    # Fallback: compute a size that fits exactly under budget
    max_pixels = max(1, budget // max(1, bpp))
    # Make it roughly square
    side = int(max(1, min(64, int(max_pixels ** 0.5))))
    w = side
    h = max(1, min(40, max_pixels // max(1, w)))
    return w, h


def _gen_gray(r: random.Random, w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    mode = r.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 0:
        # uniform
        val = r.randint(0, 255)
        return bytes([val]) * (w * h)
    elif mode == 1:
        # horizontal gradient
        row = bytearray(w)
        for x in range(w):
            row[x] = int(255 * x / max(1, w - 1))
        return bytes(row) * h
    elif mode == 2:
        # checkerboard
        vals = [0, 255]
        out = bytearray(w * h)
        idx = 0
        for y in range(h):
            for x in range(w):
                out[idx] = vals[(x + y) & 1]
                idx += 1
        return bytes(out)
    else:
        # random noise but deterministic by seed
        return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(w * h))


def _pack_channels(rgba: Tuple[int, int, int, int], fmt: str) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    r, g, b, a = rgba
    if fmt == "RGB":
        return r, g, b, a
    if fmt == "BGR":
        return b, g, r, a
    if fmt == "RGBA":
        return r, g, b, a
    if fmt == "BGRA":
        return b, g, r, a
    # default
    return r, g, b, a


def _gen_color(r: random.Random, w: int, h: int, fmt: str, bpp: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a palette
    palette = r.choice(PALETTES)
    # Patterns: solid, row stripes, col stripes, checker, gradient
    pattern = r.randint(0, 4)
    out = bytearray(w * h * bpp)
    idx = 0
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            if pattern == 0:
                p = palette[0]
            elif pattern == 1:
                p = palette[(y // max(1, h // max(1, len(palette)))) % len(palette)]
            elif pattern == 2:
                p = palette[(x // max(1, w // max(1, len(palette)))) % len(palette)]
            elif pattern == 3:
                p = palette[(x + y) % len(palette)]
            else:
                # gradient across X and Y on RGB, keep A opaque
                rx = int(255 * x / max(1, w - 1))
                gy = int(255 * y / max(1, h - 1))
                bx = 255 - rx
                p = (rx, gy, bx, 255)
            pr, pg, pb, pa = _pack_channels(p, fmt)
            if bpp == 3:
                out[idx] = pr; out[idx+1] = pg; out[idx+2] = pb; idx += 3
            else:  # 4
                out[idx] = pr; out[idx+1] = pg; out[idx+2] = pb; out[idx+3] = pa; idx += 4
    return bytes(out)

    budget = r.choice([1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096])

    w, h = _choose_size(r, bpp, budget)

    # It will be consumed with various (w,h,type) choices in the stubs; many will fit
    # or the stub adapts h based on available size. Our buffer is valid pixel data.
    return buf

def _make_nv21(w: int, h: int, pattern: bytes) -> bytes:
    # NV21 = Y plane (w*h bytes) + interleaved VU (w*h/2 bytes), chroma at half resolution
    y_size = w * h
    uv_w = w // 2
    uv_h = h // 2
    vu_size = uv_w * uv_h * 2  # each 2x2 luma block has 2 chroma bytes (V then U)

    # Build Y plane with a luminance ramp/patterned texture
    y = bytearray(y_size)
    if not pattern:
        pattern = b"\x80"
    plen = len(pattern)

    # Use a spatially varying pattern to produce non-flat images
    idx = 0
    for yrow in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            base = pattern[(idx + x + yrow * 3) % plen]
            # Slight gradient and wrap to 0..255
            y[idx] = (base + (x * 3 + yrow * 5)) & 0xFF
            idx += 1

    # Build VU interleaved plane with plausible chroma content
    vu = bytearray(vu_size)
    idx = 0
    for yrow in range(uv_h):
        for x in range(uv_w):
            # alternate chroma values to stress different hues
            v = (pattern[(idx * 2 + 0) % plen] + (x * 7)) & 0xFF
            u = (pattern[(idx * 2 + 1) % plen] + (yrow * 11)) & 0xFF
            vu[idx * 2 + 0] = v
            vu[idx * 2 + 1] = u
            idx += 1

    return bytes(y + vu)

def _choose_even(n: int) -> int:
    # ensure even to keep chroma dimensions integral
    return n if (n % 2 == 0) else n - 1

def _interesting_dims(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Fuzzer stub limits to [2..65], but src size uses exact w,h chosen inside stub.
    # We only need to provide a seed buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR; however, creating
    # representative NV21 images here makes the repeated pattern in the stub meaningful.
    candidates = [
        (2, 2), (4, 2), (8, 8), (16, 12), (32, 32), (64, 64),
        (10, 14), (18, 22), (30, 26), (50, 28), (62, 18)
    ]
    w, h = rng.choice(candidates)
    return _choose_even(w), _choose_even(h)

def _make_pattern_bank(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Provide multiple short patterns the stub will repeat across the NV21 source
    bank: List[bytes] = []
    bank.append(bytes([0x10, 0x80, 0xF0]))  # low/mid/high
    bank.append(bytes([0x00, 0xFF]))        # extreme contrast
    bank.append(bytes(range(16)))           # ramp
    bank.append(b"NV21!")                   # ASCII marker
    # Random small patterns of varying lengths (coprime to common sizes)
    for _ in range(4):
        ln = rng.choice([3,5,7,9,13])
        bank.append(bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(ln)))
    return bank

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a small suite of NV21 images concatenated, so the fuzz param string
    # provides rich repeating content regardless of src_size modulo
    w, h = _interesting_dims(rng)
    patterns = _make_pattern_bank(rng)

    blobs: List[bytes] = []
    total_cap = 0
    # Build several NV21 buffers with different patterns and possibly different dims
    for i, pat in enumerate(patterns):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            ww, hh = w, h
        else:
            # slight variation while keeping even
            ww = _choose_even(max(2, min(64, w + rng.choice([-6, -2, 2, 6]))))
            hh = _choose_even(max(2, min(64, h + rng.choice([-6, -2, 2, 6]))))
        nv21 = _make_nv21(ww, hh, pat)
        blobs.append(nv21)
        total_cap += len(nv21)
        if total_cap > 2048:  # keep output modest; stub only uses pattern modulo
            break

    # Concatenate into one buffer; the stub will cycle over this pattern to fill its src
    data = b"".join(blobs)
    # Ensure non-empty and bounded
    if not data:
        data = _make_nv21(2, 2, b"\x80\x80")
    return data[:4096]

def _nv12_make(w: int, h: int, pattern: bytes) -> bytes:
    # NV12 layout: Y plane (w*h), then interleaved UV plane (w*h/2)
    y_size = w * h
    uv_size = w * h // 2
    if not pattern:
        pattern = b"\x80"  # neutral chroma if empty
    # Build Y plane: choose a luminance gradient or pattern repetition
    y = bytearray(y_size)
    for i in range(y_size):
        y[i] = pattern[i % len(pattern)]
    # Build UV plane: interleaved U,V pairs; try to keep within valid 0..255
    uv = bytearray(uv_size)
    for i in range(0, uv_size, 2):
        p = pattern[(i // 2) % len(pattern)]
        # derive U and V from pattern with simple transforms
        u = (p + 32) & 0xFF
        v = (255 - p) & 0xFF
        uv[i] = u
        if i + 1 < uv_size:
            uv[i + 1] = v
    return bytes(y + uv)

# Predefined interesting NV12 scenarios
def _patterns() -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        bytes([0x00]),                  # black/low Y
        bytes([0xFF]),                  # white/high Y
        bytes([0x10]),                  # BT.601 dark
        bytes([0xEB]),                  # BT.601 bright
        bytes([0x80]),                  # neutral mid
        b"\x00\xFF",                   # alternating extremes
        b"\x7F\x80\x81",               # around mid
        bytes(range(16, 16+8)),         # small ramp
        bytes([29, 76, 150, 225]),      # varied luminance
        b"YUV!seeded"                   # ASCII pattern
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Generate a valid NV12 (YUV420sp) buffer suitable for ncnn::yuv420sp2rgb_nv12.
    The fuzzer stub chooses w,h in [2..65]; we mirror that range to increase
    chance of alignment and exercise different sizes. Output size is w*h*3/2.
    The returned bytes are intended to be fed to FUZZ_PARAM_STR to populate
    the YUV source buffer; the stub will repeat as needed to fill src_size.
    """
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose width/height with variety: small, odd, even, multiples of 8/16
    choices = [
        (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 4), (7, 5), (8, 8), (15, 9), (16, 16),
        (17, 33), (31, 29), (32, 32), (48, 36), (63, 65), (65, 65)
    ]
    w, h = rnd.choice(choices)

    # Compose a base pattern from predefined and some random bytes
    pats = _patterns()
    base = bytearray(rnd.choice(pats))

    # Mix in a short random tail to diversify while remaining valid
    extra_len = rnd.randint(0, 32)
    for _ in range(extra_len):
        base.append(rnd.randrange(0, 256))

    nv12 = _nv12_make(w, h, bytes(base))

    # Ensure size <= 4096; if too large, shrink by picking smaller dims deterministically
    if len(nv12) > 4096:
        # fallback to minimal legal size 2x2
        nv12 = _nv12_make(2, 2, bytes(base))

    return nv12

from typing import List

# This generator targets ASCII text inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the stubs.
# Goals:
# - Produce NUL-terminated or safely C-string-compatible buffers (framework typically makes std::string,
#   but ensuring ASCII and diverse content helps trigger font/layout code paths).
# - Include a mix of printable ASCII, whitespace, punctuation, and edge-case characters.
# - Vary lengths to exercise small/medium/long strings while staying under 4096 bytes total.
# - Occasionally include multiple lines and very long words to probe glyph advance and wrapping logic.
# - Avoid invalid encodings; stick to 7-bit ASCII to ensure validity.

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
CONTROL_EDGE = ["\t", "\n", "\r"]

def _rand_weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[float]) -> str:
    assert len(items) == len(weights)
    total = sum(weights)
    x = rng.random() * total
    acc = 0.0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def _gen_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a word with mixed cases and digits/punct occasionally
    styles = [
        (string.ascii_lowercase, 0.45),
        (string.ascii_uppercase, 0.15),
        (string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 0.25),
        (string.ascii_letters + "-_", 0.10),
        (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./", 0.05),
    ]
    alphabet = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, [s for s, _ in styles], [w for _, w in styles])
    # Length skew: many short, some long
    lens = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,12,16,24,32,48,64]
    weights = [12,10,9,8,7,6,6,6,5,4,3,2,1,1]
    L = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, lens, weights)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(L))

def _gen_sentence(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a sentence of random words with punctuation and spaces
    n_words = rng.randint(1, 20)
    words = []
    for i in range(n_words):
        w = _gen_word(rng)
        # Occasionally insert numbers or hex-like tokens
        if rng.random() < 0.08:
            w += rng.choice(["123", "0xFF", "42", "3.14", "-7"]) 
        words.append(w)
    s = " ".join(words)
    # Random punctuation at end
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s += rng.choice([".", "!", "?", ":", ";"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ""
    # Occasionally inject tabs within sentence
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        s = s.replace(" ", "\t", 1)
    return s

def _gen_multiline(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    lines = []
    while True:
        # mix of sentence and long word lines
        if rng.random() < 0.75:
            ln = _gen_sentence(rng)
        else:
            ln = _gen_word(rng)
            # create very long unbroken word sometimes to stress glyph advance
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                extra = rng.randint(16, 128)
                ln += "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(extra))
        lines.append(ln)
        cur = "\n".join(lines)
        if len(cur) >= target_len:
            break
        if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(lines) > 1:
            # stop early sometimes
            break
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _ensure_ascii(s: str) -> str:
    # Strip/replace any non-ascii just in case
    return s.encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode('ascii', 'ignore')

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a scenario
    scen = _rand_weighted_choice(
        rng,
        [
            "short_word",
            "single_sentence",
            "paragraph",
            "multiline_banner",
            "punctuation_heavy",
            "whitespace_mix",
            "long_word",
            "ascii_range",
        ],
        [
            0.15,
            0.25,
            0.2,
            0.1,
            0.1,
            0.08,
            0.07,
            0.05,
        ],
    )

    if scen == "short_word":
        s = _gen_word(rng)
    elif scen == "single_sentence":
        s = _gen_sentence(rng)
    elif scen == "paragraph":
        # 2-6 sentences separated by spaces
        ns = rng.randint(2, 6)
        s = " ".join(_gen_sentence(rng) for _ in range(ns))
    elif scen == "multiline_banner":
        target_len = rng.randint(32, 512)
        s = _gen_multiline(rng, target_len)
    elif scen == "punctuation_heavy":
        tokens = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 80)):
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                tokens.append(rng.choice(string.punctuation))
            else:
                tokens.append(rng.choice(PRINTABLE))
        s = "".join(tokens)
    elif scen == "whitespace_mix":
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40)):
            parts.append(_gen_word(rng))
            parts.append(rng.choice([" ", "\t", "\n"]))
        s = "".join(parts)
    elif scen == "long_word":
        base = _gen_word(rng)
        extra = rng.randint(64, 512)
        base += "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(extra))
        s = base
    else:  # ascii_range
        # Sample broadly across printable ASCII and a few control edges
        chars = []
        n = rng.randint(16, 512)
        for _ in range(n):
            if rng.random() < 0.05:
                chars.append(rng.choice(CONTROL_EDGE))
            else:
                chars.append(rng.choice(PRINTABLE))
        s = "".join(chars)

    # Occasionally prepend/append spaces to test leading/trailing whitespace handling
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = (" " * rng.randint(0, 3)) + s + (" " * rng.randint(0, 3))

    # Ensure ASCII-only and cap size
    s = _ensure_ascii(s)
    max_len = 4000  # leave room under 4096
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]

    # Return as bytes; std::string in stubs consumes as ASCII and uses c_str()
    return s.encode('ascii', 'strict')

import struct
from typing import List

# Target datatype: a file with arbitrary binary data
# Fuzzer stubs open the path and create a DataReaderFromStdio.
# There is no required structure, but we can provide diverse, interesting yet valid
# binary payloads that exercise different read sizes and patterns commonly used by ncnn
# when loading params/models (text-like, binary-like, aligned blocks, mixed content).

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _aligned_chunks(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct data as a sequence of length-prefixed chunks with 4-byte alignment
    # to mimic how some binary readers fetch blocks.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
        # choose a chunk size with some alignment-friendly values
        size_choices = [4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, rng.randint(5, 256)]
        sz = min(rng.choice(size_choices), MAX_SIZE - total - 8)
        if sz <= 0:
            break
        payload = _rand(rng, sz)
        parts.append(struct.pack('<I', sz))
        parts.append(payload)
        total += 4 + sz
        # pad to 4-byte alignment
        pad = (-total) & 3
        if pad:
            parts.append(b"\x00" * pad)
            total += pad
    return b"".join(parts)


def _text_param_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # NCNN has a plaintext param format; we approximate with ASCII lines and numbers.
    # Even if not parsed, it gives the reader human-readable lines and mixed digits.
    lines: List[str] = []
    # header-ish
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append("7767517\n")  # common magic in ncnn plain param
    layer_count = rng.randint(1, 10)
    blob_count = rng.randint(1, 12)
    lines.append(f"{layer_count} {blob_count}\n")
    for i in range(layer_count):
        # type id/name-ish and some integers
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            tname = rng.choice(["Convolution", "ReLU", "Pooling", "BinaryOp", "InnerProduct"])  # plausible names
        else:
            tname = str(rng.randint(0, 100))
        name = f"l{i}"
        bottoms = rng.randint(0, min(2, i))
        tops = rng.randint(1, 2)
        lines.append(f"{tname} {name} {bottoms} {tops}\n")
        # some param id=value pairs; ids within small range
        kvs = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 5)):
            pid = rng.randint(0, 15)
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                val = str(rng.randint(-23300, 65535))
            else:
                val = f"{rng.uniform(-3.0, 3.0):.6f}"
            kvs.append(f"{pid}={val}")
        if kvs:
            lines.append(" ".join(kvs) + "\n")
    text = "".join(lines).encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    # Add some binary tail to exercise read() into buffers
    tail = _rand(rng, rng.randint(16, 128))
    return (text + tail)[:MAX_SIZE]


def _modelbin_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a stream of raw floats/half/int8 blocks preceded by counts to mimic weight blobs
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    nblobs = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(nblobs):
        etype = rng.choice([1, 2, 3])  # 1=float32,2=float16,3=int8
        count = rng.randint(1, 256)
        header = struct.pack('<II', etype, count)
        blob: bytes
        if etype == 1:
            vals = [rng.uniform(-10.0, 10.0) for _ in range(count)]
            blob = b"".join(struct.pack('<f', v) for v in vals)
        elif etype == 2:
            # pack float16 via Python: use struct for half if available; else manual
            try:
                blob = b"".join(struct.pack('<e', rng.uniform(-5.0, 5.0)) for _ in range(count))
            except struct.error:
                # fallback: round float32 bytes to 2 bytes by truncation (still arbitrary bytes)
                blob = b"".join(struct.pack('<f', rng.uniform(-5.0, 5.0))[:2] for _ in range(count))
        else:
            blob = bytes((rng.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(count)))
        chunk = header + blob
        if total + len(chunk) > MAX_SIZE:
            break
        parts.append(chunk)
        total += len(chunk)
        # occasional alignment padding
        pad = (-total) & rng.choice([0, 1, 3])  # sometimes 4-align
        if pad:
            parts.append(b"\x00" * pad)
            total += pad
    return b"".join(parts)


def _mixed(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Combine different patterns to diversify access patterns
    sections = []
    for builder in rng.sample([_text_param_like, _aligned_chunks, _modelbin_like], k=rng.randint(2, 3)):
        blob = builder(rng)
        sections.append(struct.pack('<I', len(blob)))
        sections.append(blob)
    data = b"".join(sections)
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among several styles; all produce arbitrary but structured-ish bytes
    style = rng.choices(
        population=[_text_param_like, _aligned_chunks, _modelbin_like, _mixed, _rand],
        weights=[3, 2, 3, 2, 1],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if style is _rand:
        size = rng.randint(1, MAX_SIZE)
        return _rand(rng, size)

    data = style(rng)
    if len(data) == 0:
        # ensure non-empty file
        data = _rand(rng, rng.randint(1, 64))
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for NCNN binary param (.param.bin) format
# This script crafts a small but valid network graph with a few layers and blobs
# sufficient for Net::load_param_bin(dr) to succeed. We adhere to the binary
# layout used by ncnn:
#   magic (uint32) = 0x0000C0C1
#   for each layer i=0..layer_count-1
#     typeindex (int32)
#     bottoms_n (int32)  -- number of input blob indices
#     tops_n (int32)     -- number of output blob indices
#     bottoms[bottoms_n] (int32)
#     tops[tops_n] (int32)
#     param_count (int32)
#     repeated param entries:
#        id (int32)
#        type (int32)   0=int,1=float,2=string,3=array
#        value ... depending on type
#          int: int32
#          float: float32
#          string: length(int32), then bytes including trailing '\0'
#          array: elemcount(int32), then elemcount floats (float32)
#
# We do not embed names (that is for text param; binary param does not need names).
# The layer typeindex values correspond to built-in layers from layer_type_enum.h.
# Common indices (as of ncnn) used here:
#   0 = Input, 2 = Convolution, 3 = ReLU, 1 = Data, 15 = Pooling, 5 = InnerProduct
# We will only use safe/common ones: Input(0), Convolution(2), ReLU(3), Pooling(15), InnerProduct(5).
# Note: Only parameters are defined here; weights are in model.bin and are NOT required by load_param_bin.

MAGIC = 0x0000C0C1

# Helper encoders

def w_i32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<i', int(v))

def w_u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', int(v))

def w_f32(v: float) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<f', float(v))

# Parameter entry encoders according to binary param format

def p_int(pid: int, val: int) -> bytes:
    return w_i32(pid) + w_i32(0) + w_i32(val)

def p_float(pid: int, val: float) -> bytes:
    return w_i32(pid) + w_i32(1) + w_f32(val)

def p_string(pid: int, s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8') + b'\x00'
    return w_i32(pid) + w_i32(2) + w_i32(len(b)) + b

def p_array(pid: int, arr: List[float]) -> bytes:
    out = w_i32(pid) + w_i32(3) + w_i32(len(arr))
    for v in arr:
        out += w_f32(v)
    return out

# Layer builders

def layer_header(typeindex: int, bottoms: List[int], tops: List[int]) -> bytes:
    b = w_i32(typeindex)
    b += w_i32(len(bottoms))
    b += w_i32(len(tops))
    for x in bottoms:
        b += w_i32(x)
    for x in tops:
        b += w_i32(x)
    return b

# Known parameter ids for common layers (from ncnn conventions)
# Convolution: 0=num_output, 1=kernel_w, 11=kernel_h, 2=dilation_w, 12=dilation_h,
#              3=stride_w, 13=stride_h, 4=pad_left,14=pad_top,15=pad_right,16=pad_bottom,
#              5=bias_term, 6=weight_data_size, 9=group
# Pooling: 0=pooling_type(0:Max 1:Avg), 1=kernel_w, 11=kernel_h, 2=stride_w, 12=stride_h,
#          3=pad_left,14=pad_top,15=pad_right,16=pad_bottom, 4=global_pooling, 5=pad_mode, 6=avgpool_count_include_pad
# ReLU: 0=slope
# InnerProduct: 0=num_output, 1=bias_term, 2=weight_data_size


def build_simple_graph(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Randomly choose an architecture template
    # We will keep blob indexing consistent: blobs are implicitly numbered, and we
    # only reference by index here. The real NCNN binary param expects indices that
    # match connection graph. We will design a linear graph to avoid inconsistencies.

    layers = []  # each = bytes for the layer chunk (header + param_count + params)

    blob_idx = 0

    # Layer 0: Input layer produces one output blob index 0
    # Input has no parameters typically; just declare topology.
    l0 = layer_header(0, [], [blob_idx])
    params0 = []
    layers.append(l0 + w_i32(len(params0)) + b''.join(params0))

    # Decide number of conv+relu blocks
    num_blocks = rng.randint(1, 3)

    current_blob = blob_idx

    for _ in range(num_blocks):
        # Convolution
        out_channels = rng.choice([1, 3, 8, 16, 32])
        kw = rng.choice([1, 3, 5])
        kh = rng.choice([1, 3, 5])
        sw = rng.choice([1, 2])
        sh = rng.choice([1, 2])
        pad = rng.choice([0, 1])
        bias_term = rng.choice([0, 1])
        group = 1
        weight_data_size = out_channels * kw * kh  # min placeholder; real size validated on model load, not params

        next_blob = current_blob + 1
        lh = layer_header(2, [current_blob], [next_blob])
        plist = [
            p_int(0, out_channels),
            p_int(1, kw), p_int(11, kh),
            p_int(3, sw), p_int(13, sh),
            p_int(4, pad), p_int(14, pad), p_int(15, pad), p_int(16, pad),
            p_int(5, bias_term),
            p_int(6, weight_data_size),
            p_int(9, group)
        ]
        layers.append(lh + w_i32(len(plist)) + b''.join(plist))
        current_blob = next_blob

        # Optional ReLU
        if rng.random() < 0.9:
            next_blob = current_blob + 1
            lh = layer_header(3, [current_blob], [next_blob])
            slope = 0.0 if rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.uniform(0.01, 0.3)
            plist = [p_float(0, slope)]
            layers.append(lh + w_i32(len(plist)) + b''.join(plist))
            current_blob = next_blob

        # Optional Pooling
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            next_blob = current_blob + 1
            lh = layer_header(15, [current_blob], [next_blob])
            pool_type = rng.choice([0, 1])
            kw = rng.choice([2, 3])
            kh = rng.choice([2, 3])
            sw = rng.choice([1, 2])
            sh = rng.choice([1, 2])
            pad = rng.choice([0, 1])
            plist = [
                p_int(0, pool_type),
                p_int(1, kw), p_int(11, kh),
                p_int(2, sw), p_int(12, sh),
                p_int(3, pad), p_int(14, pad), p_int(15, pad), p_int(16, pad),
                p_int(4, 0),  # global_pooling off
                p_int(5, 0),  # pad_mode default
                p_int(6, 0),  # avg include pad off
            ]
            layers.append(lh + w_i32(len(plist)) + b''.join(plist))
            current_blob = next_blob

    # Final InnerProduct (fully connected)
    next_blob = current_blob + 1
    lh = layer_header(5, [current_blob], [next_blob])
    num_out = rng.choice([1, 2, 4, 10])
    bias_term = rng.choice([0, 1])
    weight_data_size = num_out  # minimal placeholder
    plist = [p_int(0, num_out), p_int(1, bias_term), p_int(2, weight_data_size)]
    layers.append(lh + w_i32(len(plist)) + b''.join(plist))

    # Assemble file
    data = bytearray()
    data += w_u32(MAGIC)
    for chunk in layers:
        data += chunk

    # Limit size
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return bytes(data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_simple_graph(rng)
